summary: Same H. pylori-positive patient with a recorded penicillin anaphylaxis. Any regimen with amoxicillin is contraindicated; Maastricht VI: bismuth quadruple (PPI, bismuth, tetracycline, metronidazole).

inputs.chiefComplaint: Follow-up of upper abdominal burning — stool test result
inputs.hpi: Review with the result of the H. pylori stool antigen test (positive). Still has post-prandial burning. No alarm features. Anaphylaxis to penicillin aged 19 (throat swelling, needed adrenaline).

exam.abdomen: Soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no mass.

inputs.socialHistory: Nurse. Non-smoker. Coffee 4 cups a day. Alcohol occasional.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Helicobacter pylori gastritis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: H. pylori-positive dyspepsia (stool antigen positive) — eradication therapy and test of cure.

mustInclude.proposedFix: As h-pylori-positive-eradication; add the bismuth quadruple (tetracycline + metronidazole) regimen.

mustExclude.proposedFix: buildPlanText / protocol medications: filter or flag drugs that match a recorded allergy class (penicillins); same finding as the seed appendicitis/cholangitis vignettes.

guideline.name: Maastricht VI/Florence consensus report — management of Helicobacter pylori infection
guideline.section: Penicillin allergy: bismuth quadruple therapy (PPI + bismuth + tetracycline + metronidazole) for 14 days
guideline.citation: Malfertheiner P, Megraud F, Rokkas T, et al. Gut. 2022;71:1724–1762.

rationale: Allergy permutation: the engines already know the allergy (header banner) but the plan templates may still print amoxicillin-based triple therapy. A contraindicated drug in a documented anaphylaxis is a patient-safety failure.
